questionText:

Illustrating an episode from the Tenth Canto of the Bhagavata Purana, the painting portrays the pastoral migration of the cowherd community of Gokul across the sacred river Yamuna to seek safety and greener pastures in the idyllic groves of Vrindavana, escaping the demons sent by tyrant King Kamsa. The monumental folio is a breathtaking triumph of lyrical naturalism: covered bullock carts carry household possessions, women, and infants, while cowherd youths herd cattle through the shallow river waters.
